_doc: Riddle stones and riddlers (PuzzleSpots.gd, docs/PUZZLES.md). Placed here, never in the map files. at: tablet (a carved stone, PuzzleTablet) or npc (a riddler, sprite). kind: pick, type, order, listen, lights, slide, push, steps. Texts are English keys translated through tools/i18n (table puzzle_spots); typed answers list the accepted words per language. chain parts give a clue line; needs lists the parts a chain's last stone waits for. reward: item/count, coins, look (lantern flame in lantern_colors.json, unlocked by flag pz_<id>), meet (rare wild Spirling on map, default the spot's map).

spots.title: Keeper's Stone I
spots.text: A riddle is cut into the stone: I have a round face but never smile, and two hands but never wave. I tell you when it is time to go home. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Think of something that keeps time.
spots.hint_2: Its hands go round and round.
spots.clue: I am kept on a hill, but I watch the sea.

spots.title: Keeper's Stone II
spots.text: Four small bells hang over the stone. They ring a short song. Ring it back to them.
spots.hint_1: Watch which bell lights up, not only the sound.
spots.hint_2: The song starts with the gold bell and ends with the red one.
spots.clue: I sleep all day and work all night.

spots.title: Keeper's Stone III
spots.text: Nine lamp stones are set in the wall. Light all nine. Each tap also flips the stones next to it.
spots.hint_1: Each stone needs one tap at most, and the order does not matter.
spots.hint_2: Tap the top left corner, the bottom right corner and the middle stone.
spots.clue: Ships thank me, but they never come to visit.

spots.title: The Keeper's Answer
spots.text: Three stones in Veydal each gave you a line. This stone asks: what one thing do all three lines describe?
spots.hint_1: It stands on a hill by the sea and shines at night.
spots.hint_2: Ships steer by its light, but never sail to it.

spots.title: Tracks in the Mud
spots.text: Fresh round paw prints lead off between the trees, crossed by sharp claw marks. Follow only the round prints to whoever made them.
spots.hint_1: Claw marks and bare mud both lose the trail.
spots.hint_2: Where the trail splits, the left branch is a dead end. Keep going right.

spots.title: The Four Lanterns
spots.text: Four lanterns: red, blue, green and gold. The plaque reads: The sun goes down first. Then the sea goes dark. Then the moss falls asleep. The fire rests last.
spots.hint_1: The sun is gold and the sea is blue.
spots.hint_2: Gold, then blue, then green, then red.

spots.title: The Glassblower's Floor
spots.text: Chalk marks on the floor and two heavy slag blocks. A note beside them: Cover both marks, and my first line is yours.
spots.hint_1: A block pushed against a wall can only slide along it.
spots.hint_2: Push the left block down twice, then push it left along the bottom.
spots.clue: I am made of sand, yet you can see right through me.

spots.title: The Glassblower's Riddle
spots.text: Scratched into a cooled slab: What is left when fire has eaten everything? I am grey and light as a feather, and the wind carries me away.
spots.hint_1: Look in any cold fireplace.
spots.hint_2: It is grey and soft, and it is left over after burning.
spots.clue: Heat me hot enough and I glow and run like honey.

spots.title: The Glassblower's Will
spots.text: The glassblower's last stone. Two lines lead here, one about sand and one about heat. Name what the glassblower made.
spots.hint_1: You look through it every day, in every window.
spots.hint_2: It is clear and breaks if you drop it.

spots.title: The Kiln Vents
spots.text: Sixteen vents in an old kiln wall. Open every vent to warm the stone. Each tap also flips the vents beside it.
spots.hint_1: Tapping a vent twice undoes it, so each vent needs one tap at most.
spots.hint_2: Start with the top left corner and the bottom right corner.

spots.title: The Stationmaster's Riddle
spots.text: The stationmaster grins: I hold every road in Ashmere, yet I weigh less than a sparrow. Fold me, and the mountains bend. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Travellers unfold it to find their way.
spots.hint_2: Roads and mountains are drawn on it.

spots.title: The Dyers' Rhyme
spots.text: Four dye vats: red, blue, yellow and black. A rhyme is painted on the wall: Yellow starts the day. Blue comes before red. Black always comes last.
spots.hint_1: Yellow is first and black is last.
spots.hint_2: Yellow, blue, red, black.

spots.title: The Pond Stone
spots.text: A mossy stone by the pond: I fall all day but never break a bone. I drum on every roof but have no hands. The ponds drink me and grow fat. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Look up on a grey day.
spots.hint_2: It comes from the clouds and fills the ponds.

spots.title: The Rooks' Call
spots.text: Four rooks sit on the wall and call in turn. Call back the same song, and they will show you a shy friend of theirs.
spots.hint_1: The song is five calls long.
spots.hint_2: It starts and ends with the grey rook.

spots.title: The Harbour Picture
spots.text: A tile picture of the harbour, all mixed up. Slide the tiles until the numbers run from 1 to 8.
spots.hint_1: Tap a tile next to the gap to slide it.
spots.hint_2: Finish the top row first, then the rest.

spots.title: The Woad Barrels
spots.text: Two dye barrels and two drain plates on an old jetty. Roll each barrel onto a plate.
spots.hint_1: Never push a barrel into a corner, it will not come out again.
spots.hint_2: Walk down the left side and along the bottom, then push the right barrel one step right.

spots.title: The Sun Tablet
spots.text: In the morning I am long. At noon I am almost gone. In the evening I am long again, and I always lie on the side away from the sun. What am I?
spots.hint_1: You take it with you wherever you walk in the sun.
spots.hint_2: It is dark, and it has your shape.

spots.title: Tracks in the Sand
spots.text: Small hoof prints cross the sand, and lizard tracks wind all around them. Follow only the hoof prints.
spots.hint_1: The hoof prints never touch the lizard tracks.
spots.hint_2: Step right once, then follow the prints up and along the top.

spots.title: The Dome Mirrors
spots.text: Nine mirrors under the dome. Turn every one of them to the sun. Each tap also turns the mirrors beside it.
spots.hint_1: Each mirror needs one tap at most.
spots.hint_2: One tap belongs in the middle of the top row.

spots.title: The Caravan Master's Riddle
spots.text: The caravan master says: In the desert people pay gold for me. In the rain they grumble about me. I have no colour and no taste, yet a whole caravan stops for me. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Every well is full of it.
spots.hint_2: You drink it when you are thirsty.

spots.title: Ledger Stone I
spots.text: A clerk's riddle: Each day a clerk writes twice as many names as the day before. On the tenth day the page is full. On which day was it half full?
spots.hint_1: Work backwards from the full page.
spots.hint_2: One day before it was full, it held half as many names.
spots.clue: What you seek keeps every name, yet never says one aloud.

spots.title: Ledger Stone II
spots.text: A printer's plate cut into nine squares, one of them missing. Slide the squares back so the numbers run from 1 to 8.
spots.hint_1: Tap a square next to the gap to slide it.
spots.hint_2: Put 1, 2 and 3 in the top row first.
spots.clue: It sleeps on a shelf, with a hard back and many leaves.

spots.title: The Icicle Chimes
spots.text: Four icicles hang from the eaves and chime in the cold wind. Chime the same tune back, and something on the moor will hear it.
spots.hint_1: Watch the icicles light up as they ring.
spots.hint_2: The tune starts on the white icicle and has five notes.

spots.title: The Press Bed
spots.text: Three type blocks lie on the press bed, and three marks show where they belong. Push each block onto a mark.
spots.hint_1: A block in a corner is stuck for good. Use Reset if that happens.
spots.hint_2: Walk right twice, then push the block above you up.

spots.title: The Postmaster's Riddle
spots.text: The postmaster taps the counter: I ride on every letter to the far shore, but I stay in one corner the whole way. Lick me once and I hold on for life. What am I?
spots.hint_1: You buy it at the post office.
spots.hint_2: It is a small paper square stuck on a letter.

spots.title: Ledger Stone III
spots.text: Nine candles stand in a niche of the wall. Light all nine. Each tap also flips the candles beside it.
spots.hint_1: Each candle needs one tap at most.
spots.hint_2: Two of the taps are in the bottom row.
spots.clue: Open it, and it speaks to you without a sound.

spots.title: The Ledger's Answer
spots.text: Two lines came from Quillmarch and one from Tallowmarket. What keeps every name, sleeps on a shelf and speaks without a sound?
spots.hint_1: It has pages.
spots.hint_2: A library is full of them.

spots.title: The Lock Gates
spots.text: Four gate wheels: white, red, green and grey. The keeper's song: Green holds back the sea, so green turns first. Grey sits just above green. White is the top gate. Red sits between grey and white.
spots.hint_1: Green turns first and white turns last.
spots.hint_2: Green, grey, red, white.

spots.title: The Mask Maker's Riddle
spots.text: The mask maker smiles: I go to every ball and show a face, but there is no head behind me. I smile all night and never get tired. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Look at what this person makes.
spots.hint_2: You wear it over your face.

spots.title: Tracks in the Reeds
spots.text: Webbed prints lead into the marsh, and eel trails wind across them. Follow only the webbed prints.
spots.hint_1: Eel trails and bare mud both lose the trail.
spots.hint_2: Go down the left edge first.

spots.title: The Ridge Orrery
spots.text: A small orrery with four worlds: blue, white, gold and red. The plaque: The small red world is closest to the sun. The gold one comes next. Blue follows gold. The pale white one keeps farthest out. Set them from the sun outward.
spots.hint_1: Red is closest to the sun.
spots.hint_2: Red, gold, blue, white.

spots.title: The Starwell Tablet
spots.text: At night I am everywhere you look up. By day I hide, though I never leave. Sailors steer by me. What am I?
spots.hint_1: Look up on a clear night.
spots.hint_2: This town is named after them.

spots.title: The Flat Mirrors
spots.text: Sixteen mirrors lie in the salt. Turn them all to face the sky. Each tap also turns the mirrors beside it.
spots.hint_1: Each mirror needs one tap at most.
spots.hint_2: Two of the taps are in the bottom row, side by side.

spots.title: The Wind Chimes
spots.text: Five chimes hang from a bent tree, and the wind plays a tune on them. Play it back, and something shy might come to listen.
spots.hint_1: The tune is six notes long.
spots.hint_2: It starts on the green chime.

spots.title: The Gilt Tiles
spots.text: Nine gilt tiles in a frame, and one of them is missing. Slide them until the numbers run from 1 to 8.
spots.hint_1: Tap a tile next to the gap to slide it.
spots.hint_2: Finish the top row first, then the left column.
